text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 25 in history:
1306 - Robert de Bruce was crowned Robert I the Bruce of Scotland. He led the forces that freed Scotland from English rule in 1328.
1799 - The Austrians defeated the French at the Battle of Stokach in the French Revolutionary Wars.
1807 - The slave trade in England was abolished.

1867 - Arturo Toscanini, Italian conductor and musical director, born. Famed for his temper in rehearsals, he was director of La Scala and the Metropolitan opera houses. He also conducted the NBC symphony orchestra.
1871 - Gutzon Borglum, U.S. sculptor famed for his presidential sculptures on Mount Rushmore, born.

1881 - Bela Bartok, Hungarian composer and pianist, born. His knowledge of western musical techniques allied to the inspiration he derived from Hungarian peasant songs enabled him to become a unique musical force.
1895 - Italian troops invaded Abyssinia (Ethiopia).
1906 - Professor Alan John Percivale Taylor, English historian, born. His "Origins of the Second World War" aroused passionate hostility among other historians.
1911 - 146 mostly young Jewish and Italian immigrant women died when New York's worst industrial fire swept through a factory owned by the Triangle Shirtwaist Co.

1914 - Frederic Mistral, French poet and winner of the 1904 Nobel Prize for Literature, died. He helped in the 19th century revival of Provencal language and worked for some 20 years on a Provencal-French dictionary.
1918 - French composer Claude Debussy died. His music, described as "musical Impressionism", explored original avenues of expression.
1924 - King George of Greece was deposed and a republic proclaimed.
1935 - Paul Van Zeeland became premier of Belgium.
1941 - Yugoslavia joined the Tripartite Pact, a military alliance directed against the U.S. and Britain.
1947 - Elton John, English singer, songwriter and pianist, born. An extremely successful pop-rock star, in 1979 he became the first western pop musician to play in Russia.
1949 - Laurence Olivier's "Hamlet" won five Oscars in becoming the first British film to win an Academy award.
1957 - The Treaty of Rome was signed, providing for the setting up, from 1 January 1958, of the Common Market in Europe.
1975 - King Faisal of Saudi Arabia was murdered by his nephew Prince Faisal. He was succeeded by his brother, Khaled ibn Abdul-aziz.
1980 - Archbishop Robert Runcie was enthroned as Archbishop of Canterbury.
1984 - French troops began part of a phased withdrawal of its 1,300 man peacekeeping force from Beirut.
1990 - A fire swept through a packed, unlicensed nightclub in New York killing 87 people.
1994 - The last U.S. troops left Somalia after a 15-month peace mission, leaving only a depleted U.N. force behind.
1994 - Neo-Nazis firebombed a synagogue in the north German town of Luebeck, probably the first such incident in Germany since the 1938 Nazi "Kristallnacht" pogrom.
1995 - Former heavyweight boxing champion Mike Tyson was freed from an Indiana prison three years after his conviction for rape.
1996 - Officials from the 15 EU states agreed to recommend a ban on exports of British beef products because of concern over mad cow disease.
1996 - France, Britain and the U.S. signed the South Pacific Nuclear Free Zone Treaty.
